original_question: Let chi_{8d} denote the quadratic character attached to the fundamental discriminant 8d, with d ranging over odd squarefree integers 0 < d < X. Young proved a first-moment asymptotic of the form sum L(1/2, chi_{8d}) = X P(log X) + O(X^(1/2 + epsilon)). Improve this by reducing the exponent 1/2, ideally toward a secondary term of size c X^(1/4) plus a smaller error.
target_in_paper: Problem (18) in the Problems section (page 8), containing equations (16) and (17): improve Young’s first-moment asymptotic for quadratic Dirichlet L-values over positive odd squarefree d, with the sharper target suggested by Florea involving a c X^(1/4) secondary term. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact intent: it has the right family (quadratic Dirichlet characters chi_{8d}), the correct summation set (positive odd squarefree d with fundamental discriminant 8d), Young’s asymptotic shape X P(log X) + O(X^(1/2+epsilon)), and the paper’s suggested stronger direction of a c X^(1/4) secondary term with a smaller remainder. It therefore matches Problem (18), not the neighboring fourth-moment Problem (19). ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
missing_details: State the asymptotic regime explicitly as X -> infinity. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

Spell out the summation condition in the statement itself: the sum is over integers d with 0 < d < X, d odd, and d squarefree; if one uses a starred sum, that notation must be defined. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

Specify the ambient arithmetic setting: chi_{8d} is the quadratic Dirichlet character over Q associated to the fundamental discriminant 8d. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

Make clear that P is the same polynomial appearing in Young’s asymptotic; Problem (18) does not ask to determine P and does not specify its degree there. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

Replace the vague phrase 'ideally toward' by the paper’s precise stronger target: prove or approach X P(log X) + c X^(1/4) + O(X^theta) for some real constant c and some theta in (0, 1/4). ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

Preserve the paper’s scope: the official goal is to improve Young’s result by reducing the exponent 1/2; the c X^(1/4) formula is presented as Florea’s suggested sharper phenomenon, not as an already adopted theorem. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
Do not add smoothing, extra weights, twists, or other averaging procedures; none appear in Problem (18). ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))

Homogeneity, degree restrictions of forms, nilpotency conditions, and quantifiers such as 'for all sufficiently large m' are not relevant to this problem. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
refined_question: As X -> infinity, let S(X) := sum over all integers d with 0 < d < X, d odd, and d squarefree, of L(1/2, chi_{8d}), where chi_{8d} is the quadratic Dirichlet character associated to the fundamental discriminant 8d. Young proved that S(X) = X P(log X) + O(X^(1/2+epsilon)). Improve this first-moment asymptotic by lowering the error-term exponent 1/2. Ideally, prove the sharper asymptotic suggested by Florea, namely S(X) = X P(log X) + c X^(1/4) + O(X^theta) for some constant c in R and some theta with 0 < theta < 1/4. ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Problem (18) exactly. On page 8, the paper cites Young’s first-moment result for sum_{0<d<X} L(1/2, chi_{8d}) over odd squarefree d, then immediately states Florea’s suggested refinement with a c X^(1/4) secondary term and O(X^theta) remainder, and says that 'the goal would be to improve (16) by reducing the exponent 1/2.' The introduction’s general family-moment framework (equation (14), page 2) confirms that this is being posed as a concrete central-value moment problem inside a family of L-functions, while the notation section adds no hidden conventions specific to Problem (18). So the refined question should stay narrowly focused on this unsmoothed first moment over the chi_{8d} family and should not drift to neighboring problems such as the fourth moment in Problem (19). ([personal.math.ubc.ca](https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/papers/downloads/MLPL.pdf))
